sanskrit: sarvān nānātvayuktāṃś ca sarvān pratyakṣahetukān yataḥ paraṃ na vidyeta tato 'bhyāse bhaviṣyati
english: When all things marked by diversity, and all whose causes are perceptible, are seen to be such that beyond them nothing further exists—then realization comes through sustained practice.

sanskrit: vāsudeva uvāca tatas tu tasyā brāhmaṇyā matiḥ kṣetrajñasaṃkṣaye kṣetrajñād eva parataḥ kṣetrajño 'nyaḥ pravartate
english: Vāsudeva said: Then the understanding of that Brāhmaṇī, upon the dissolution of the Knower of the Field, perceived that beyond the Knower of the Field a higher, other Knower of the Field arises.

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca kva nu sā brāhmaṇī kṛṣṇa kva cāsau brāhmaṇarṣabhaḥ yābhyāṃ siddhir iyaṃ prāptā tāv ubhau vada me 'cyuta
english: Arjuna said: Where, O Kṛṣṇa, is that Brāhmaṇī, and where that bull among Brāhmaṇas, by whom this perfection was attained? Tell me of them both, O undecaying one.

sanskrit: vāsudeva uvāca mano me brāhmaṇaṃ viddhi buddhiṃ me viddhi brāhmaṇīm kṣetrajña iti yaś coktaḥ so 'ham eva dhanaṃjaya
english: Vāsudeva said: Know my mind to be the Brāhmaṇa, and know my intellect to be the Brāhmaṇī; and he who was called the Knower of the Field—that, O Dhanaṃjaya, is none but myself.

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca brahma yat paramaṃ vedyaṃ tan me vyākhyātum arhasi bhavato hi prasādena sūkṣme me ramate matiḥ
english: Arjuna said: That supreme Brahman which is to be known—this you ought to expound to me; for by your grace my mind takes delight in things subtle.

sanskrit: vāsudeva uvāca atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam saṃvādaṃ mokṣasaṃyuktaṃ śiṣyasya guruṇā saha
english: Vāsudeva said: On this too they recount an ancient tale—a dialogue concerning liberation between a disciple and his teacher.

sanskrit: kaś cid brāhmaṇam āsīnam ācāryaṃ saṃśitavratam śiṣyaḥ papraccha medhāvī kiṃ svic chreyaḥ paraṃtapa
english: A certain wise disciple, O scorcher of foes, questioned a Brāhmaṇa teacher of firm vows, who sat at ease: 'What, indeed, is the highest good?'

sanskrit: bhagavantaṃ prapanno 'haṃ niḥśreyasaparāyaṇaḥ yāce tvāṃ śirasā vipra yad brūyāṃ tad vicakṣva me
english: 'I have taken refuge in you, my lord, intent upon the supreme good. I beseech you with bowed head, O Brāhmaṇa: explain to me that of which I would ask.'

sanskrit: tam evaṃvādinaṃ pārtha śiṣyaṃ gurur uvāca ha kathayasva pravakṣyāmi yatra te saṃśayo dvija
english: To the disciple who spoke thus, O Pārtha, the teacher replied: 'Speak forth, twice-born one; I shall declare to you that whereon your doubt lies.'

sanskrit: ity uktaḥ sa kuruśreṣṭha guruṇā guruvatsalaḥ prāñjaliḥ paripapraccha yat tac chṛṇu mahāmate
english: Thus addressed by the teacher, O best of the Kurus, that disciple, devoted to his guru, with joined palms put his question—hear it, O great-minded one.

sanskrit: śiṣya uvāca kutaś cāhaṃ kutaś ca tvaṃ tat satyaṃ brūhi yat param kuto jātāni bhūtāni sthāvarāṇi carāṇi ca
english: The disciple said: Whence am I, and whence are you? Tell me that highest truth. Whence have beings come to be, the standing and the moving alike?

sanskrit: kena jīvanti bhūtāni teṣām āyuḥ kim ātmakam kiṃ satyaṃ kiṃ tapo vipra ke guṇāḥ sadbhir īritāḥ ke panthānaḥ śivāḥ santi kiṃ sukhaṃ kiṃ ca duṣkṛtam
english: By what do beings live, and of what nature is their life-span? What is truth, what is austerity, O Brāhmaṇa? What virtues are praised by the good? Which are the auspicious paths? What is happiness, and what is wrongdoing?

sanskrit: etān me bhagavan praśnān yāthātathyena sattama vaktum arhasi viprarṣe yathāvad iha tattvataḥ
english: These my questions, O blessed and most excellent one, O sage among Brāhmaṇas, you ought to answer here truly, exactly, and in accordance with reality.

sanskrit: vāsudeva uvāca tasmai saṃpratipannāya yathāvat paripṛcchate śiṣyāya guṇayuktāya śāntāya guruvartine chāyābhūtāya dāntāya yataye brahmacāriṇe
english: Vāsudeva said: To that disciple—well-disposed, questioning fitly, endowed with virtues, tranquil, obedient to his guru, become as his very shadow, self-restrained, a striver, a chaste student—

sanskrit: tān praśnān abravīt pārtha medhāvī sa dhṛtavrataḥ guruḥ kurukulaśreṣṭha samyak sarvān ariṃdama
english: to those questions, O Pārtha, the wise teacher of steadfast vows replied—all of them rightly, O best of the Kuru line, O subduer of foes.

sanskrit: brahmaproktam idaṃ dharmam ṛṣipravarasevitam vedavidyāsamāvāpyaṃ tattvabhūtārthabhāvanam
english: The teacher said: This Law was proclaimed by Brahmā, cultivated by the foremost seers, to be attained through knowledge of the Vedas, the contemplation of the truly real.

sanskrit: bhūtabhavyabhaviṣyādidharmakāmārthaniścayam siddhasaṃghaparijñātaṃ purākalpaṃ sanātanam
english: It settles the matters of duty, desire, and gain concerning past, present, future, and the rest; it is fully known to the hosts of the perfected; it belongs to the ancient ordinance and is eternal.

sanskrit: pravakṣye 'haṃ mahāprājña padam uttamam adya te buddhvā yad iha saṃsiddhā bhavantīha manīṣiṇaḥ
english: I shall declare to you today, O greatly wise one, the supreme station, by understanding which the thoughtful become perfected here.

sanskrit: upagamyarṣayaḥ pūrvaṃ jijñāsantaḥ parasparam bṛhaspatibharadvājau gautamo bhārgavas tathā
english: Of old the seers, drawing near and seeking knowledge from one another—Bṛhaspati and Bharadvāja, Gautama and the Bhārgava as well,

sanskrit: vasiṣṭhaḥ kāśyapaś caiva viśvāmitro 'trir eva ca mārgān sarvān parikramya pariśrāntāḥ svakarmabhiḥ
english: Vasiṣṭha and Kāśyapa, and Viśvāmitra and Atri too—having traversed all the paths and grown weary through their own works,

sanskrit: ṛṣim āṅgirasaṃ vṛddhaṃ puraskṛtya tu te dvijāḥ dadṛśur brahmabhavane brahmāṇaṃ vītakalmaṣam
english: those twice-born ones, placing the aged seer of the Aṅgiras line before them, beheld in the abode of Brahmā the spotless Brahmā himself.

sanskrit: taṃ praṇamya mahātmānaṃ sukhāsīnaṃ maharṣayaḥ papracchur vinayopetā niḥśreyasam idaṃ param
english: Bowing to that great-souled one as he sat at ease, the great seers, full of humility, asked of him this supreme highest good:

sanskrit: kathaṃ karma kriyāt sādhu kathaṃ mucyeta kilbiṣāt ke no mārgāḥ śivāś ca syuḥ kiṃ satyaṃ kiṃ ca duṣkṛtam
english: 'How may action be well performed? How may one be freed from sin? Which are our auspicious paths? What is truth, and what is wrongdoing?'

sanskrit: kenobhau karmapanthānau mahattvaṃ kena vindati pralayaṃ cāpavargaṃ ca bhūtānāṃ prabhavāpyayau
english: 'By what are the two paths of action traversed? By what does one win greatness? And whence the dissolution and final release, the arising and ceasing of beings?'

sanskrit: ity uktaḥ sa muniśreṣṭhair yad āha prapitāmahaḥ tat te 'haṃ saṃpravakṣyāmi śṛṇu śiṣya yathāgamam
english: Thus questioned by those foremost sages, what the Great-grandsire said—that I shall fully declare to you. Hear it, O disciple, as it has come down.

sanskrit: brahmovāca satyād bhūtāni jātāni sthāvarāṇi carāṇi ca tapasā tāni jīvanti iti tad vitta suvratāḥ
english: Brahmā said: From truth are beings born, the standing and the moving alike; by austerity they live. Know this, O you of good vows.

sanskrit: svāṃ yoniṃ punar āgamya vartante svena karmaṇā satyaṃ hi guṇasaṃyuktaṃ niyataṃ pañcalakṣaṇam
english: Returning again to their own source, they continue on by their own deeds; for truth, joined with the virtues, is fixed and has five marks.

sanskrit: brahma satyaṃ tapaḥ satyaṃ satyaṃ caiva prajāpatiḥ satyād bhūtāni jātāni bhūtaṃ satyamayaṃ mahat
english: Brahman is truth, austerity is truth, and Prajāpati too is truth; from truth are beings born, and this great creation is made of truth.

sanskrit: tasmāt satyāśrayā viprā nityaṃ yogaparāyaṇāḥ atītakrodhasaṃtāpā niyatā dharmasetavaḥ
english: Therefore the Brāhmaṇas, having truth for their refuge, ever devoted to yoga, beyond anger and torment, self-controlled, are the very bridges of the Law.

sanskrit: anyonyaniyatān vaidyān dharmasetupravartakān tān ahaṃ saṃpravakṣyāmi śāśvatān lokabhāvanān
english: Of these learned ones, restrained toward one another, who set in motion the bridges of the Law, eternal and sustaining the worlds—of them I shall fully tell.

sanskrit: cāturvidyaṃ tathā varṇāṃś caturaś cāśramān pṛthak dharmam ekaṃ catuṣpādaṃ nityam āhur manīṣiṇaḥ
english: The fourfold knowledge, the four social orders, and the four stages of life severally—these the wise call the one eternal Law with its four supports.

sanskrit: panthānaṃ vaḥ pravakṣyāmi śivaṃ kṣemakaraṃ dvijāḥ niyataṃ brahmabhāvāya yātaṃ pūrvaṃ manīṣibhiḥ
english: I shall declare to you, O twice-born, the auspicious path that brings security, ordained for the attainment of the state of Brahman, trodden of old by the wise.

sanskrit: gadatas taṃ mamādyeha panthānaṃ durvidaṃ param nibodhata mahābhāgā nikhilena paraṃ padam
english: As I now speak of that supreme path, so hard to know, attend, O highly fortunate ones, in its entirety to the supreme station.

sanskrit: brahmacārikam evāhur āśramaṃ prathamaṃ padam gārhasthyaṃ tu dvitīyaṃ syād vānaprastham ataḥ param tataḥ paraṃ tu vijñeyam adhyātmaṃ paramaṃ padam
english: They call the stage of the chaste student the first station; the householder's life would be the second; thereafter comes the forest-dweller's; and beyond that is to be known the spiritual life, the supreme station.

sanskrit: jyotir ākāśam ādityo vāyur indraḥ prajāpatiḥ nopaiti yāvad adhyātmaṃ tāvad etān na paśyati tasyopāyaṃ pravakṣyāmi purastāt taṃ nibodhata
english: Light, ether, the Sun, the Wind, Indra, Prajāpati—so long as one does not approach the spiritual life, so long does one not behold these. The means thereto I shall declare beforehand; attend to it.

sanskrit: phalamūlānilabhujāṃ munīnāṃ vasatāṃ vane vānaprasthaṃ dvijātīnāṃ trayāṇām upadiśyate
english: For sages who feed on fruit, root, and air, dwelling in the forest, the forest-dweller's mode of life is enjoined for the three twice-born orders.

sanskrit: sarveṣām eva varṇānāṃ gārhasthyaṃ tad vidhīyate śraddhālakṣaṇam ity evaṃ dharmaṃ dhīrāḥ pracakṣate
english: For all the social orders alike the householder's life is ordained; thus the steadfast declare that Law, whose mark is faith.

sanskrit: ity ete devayānā vaḥ panthānaḥ parikīrtitāḥ sadbhir adhyāsitā dhīraiḥ karmabhir dharmasetavaḥ
english: Thus have these paths leading to the gods been proclaimed to you—trodden by the good and the steadfast, by their works the bridges of the Law.

sanskrit: eteṣāṃ pṛthag adhyāste yo dharmaṃ saṃśitavrataḥ kālāt paśyati bhūtānāṃ sadaiva prabhavāpyayau
english: Whoever, of firm vow, severally follows the Law of these stages, in due time ever beholds the arising and the ceasing of beings.

sanskrit: atas tattvāni vakṣyāmi yāthātathyena hetunā viṣayasthāni sarvāṇi vartamānāni bhāgaśaḥ
english: Now I shall declare the principles truly and with their causes—all of them abiding in their spheres, operating each in its own portion.

sanskrit: mahān ātmā tathāvyaktam ahaṃkāras tathaiva ca indriyāṇi daśaikaṃ ca mahābhūtāni pañca ca
english: The Great Self, the Unmanifest, and likewise the I-maker; the senses, ten and one besides; and the five great elements;

sanskrit: viśeṣāḥ pañcabhūtānām ity eṣā vaidikī śrutiḥ caturviṃśatir eṣā vas tattvānāṃ saṃprakīrtitā
english: and the distinctive qualities of the five elements—such is the Vedic teaching. This count of four-and-twenty principles has been declared to you.

sanskrit: tattvānām atha yo veda sarveṣāṃ prabhavāpyayau sa dhīraḥ sarvabhūteṣu na moham adhigacchati
english: Now whoever knows the arising and ceasing of all the principles—that steadfast one falls into no delusion amid any of the beings.

sanskrit: tattvāni yo vedayate yathātathaṃ; guṇāṃś ca sarvān akhilāś ca devatāḥ vidhūtapāpmā pravimucya bandhanaṃ; sa sarvalokān amalān samaśnute
english: Whoever truly knows the principles, and all the qualities, and all the deities entire—he, his sin shaken off and his bondage cast away, attains to all the stainless worlds.

sanskrit: brahmovāca tad avyaktam anudriktaṃ sarvavyāpi dhruvaṃ sthiram navadvāraṃ puraṃ vidyāt triguṇaṃ pañcadhātukam
english: Brahmā said: That Unmanifest, unagitated, all-pervading, fixed, and steadfast—one should know it as a city of nine gates, of three strands, of five elements.

sanskrit: ekādaśaparikṣepaṃ mano vyākaraṇātmakam buddhisvāmikam ity etat param ekādaśaṃ bhavet
english: Encompassed by eleven, with mind as its analyzing power and intellect as its lord—this would be that supreme eleventh.

sanskrit: trīṇi srotāṃsi yāny asminn āpyāyante punaḥ punaḥ praṇāḍyas tisra evaitāḥ pravartante guṇātmikāḥ
english: The three streams that swell within it again and again—these very three channels, made of the strands, are what flow forth.

sanskrit: tamo rajas tathā sattvaṃ guṇān etān pracakṣate anyonyamithunāḥ sarve tathānyonyānujīvinaḥ
english: Tamas, rajas, and sattva—these they call the strands. All are paired with one another, and likewise all live upon one another.

sanskrit: anyonyāpāśrayāś caiva tathānyonyānuvartinaḥ anyonyavyatiṣaktāś ca triguṇāḥ pañca dhātavaḥ
english: They lean upon one another, and follow upon one another, and are interwoven with one another—the three strands and the five elements.

sanskrit: tamaso mithunaṃ sattvaṃ sattvasya mithunaṃ rajaḥ rajasaś cāpi sattvaṃ syāt sattvasya mithunaṃ tamaḥ
english: The mate of tamas is sattva, the mate of sattva is rajas; and of rajas too the mate may be sattva, and the mate of sattva is tamas.

sanskrit: niyamyate tamo yatra rajas tatra pravartate niyamyate rajo yatra sattvaṃ tatra pravartate
english: Where tamas is restrained, there rajas comes into play; where rajas is restrained, there sattva comes into play.

sanskrit: naiśātmakaṃ tamo vidyāt triguṇaṃ mohasaṃjñitam adharmalakṣaṇaṃ caiva niyataṃ pāpakarmasu
english: One should know tamas to be of the nature of night, threefold, called delusion, marked by unrighteousness, and fixed upon evil deeds.

sanskrit: pravṛttyātmakam evāhū rajaḥ paryāyakārakam pravṛttaṃ sarvabhūteṣu dṛśyatotpattilakṣaṇam
english: Rajas they declare to be of the nature of activity, bringing things about in turn; engaged in all beings, it is seen, marked by origination.

sanskrit: prakāśaṃ sarvabhūteṣu lāghavaṃ śraddadhānatā sāttvikaṃ rūpam evaṃ tu lāghavaṃ sādhusaṃmitam
english: Illumination in all beings, lightness, faithfulness—such is the form of sattva; and this lightness is esteemed by the good.

sanskrit: eteṣāṃ guṇatattvaṃ hi vakṣyate hetvahetubhiḥ samāsavyāsayuktāni tattvatas tāni vitta me
english: The true nature of these strands shall be told with reasons and counter-reasons; with their parts combined and analyzed, know them from me in their reality.

sanskrit: saṃmoho 'jñānam atyāgaḥ karmaṇām avinirṇayaḥ svapnaḥ stambho bhayaṃ lobhaḥ śokaḥ sukṛtadūṣaṇam
english: Bewilderment, ignorance, non-renunciation, indecision in deeds; sleep, stupor, fear, greed, grief, the spoiling of good works;

sanskrit: asmṛtiś cāvipākaś ca nāstikyaṃ bhinnavṛttitā nirviśeṣatvam andhatvaṃ jaghanyaguṇavṛttitā
english: forgetfulness, immaturity of judgment, unbelief, inconstancy of conduct, lack of discernment, blindness, the practice of the basest qualities;

sanskrit: akṛte kṛtamānitvam ajñāne jñānamānitā amaitrī vikṛto bhāvo aśraddhā mūḍhabhāvanā
english: thinking a thing done that is undone, fancying oneself knowing where there is no knowledge, unfriendliness, a perverted disposition, faithlessness, deluded imagining;

sanskrit: anārjavam asaṃjñatvaṃ karma pāpam acetanā gurutvaṃ sannabhāvatvam asitatvam avāg gatiḥ
english: crookedness, want of consciousness, sinful action, insentience, heaviness, a state of collapse, darkness, a downward course;

sanskrit: sarva ete guṇā viprās tāmasāḥ saṃprakīrtitāḥ ye cānye niyatā bhāvā loke 'smin mohasaṃjñitāḥ
english: all these qualities, O Brāhmaṇas, are declared to belong to tamas, together with whatever other settled states in this world are called delusion.

sanskrit: tatra tatra niyamyante sarve te tāmasā guṇāḥ parivādakathā nityaṃ devabrāhmaṇavaidikāḥ
english: In this case and that, all those qualities of tamas are reckoned, as is the constant speech that reviles the gods, the Brāhmaṇas, and the Vedas.

sanskrit: atyāgaś cābhimānaś ca moho manyus tathākṣamā matsaraś caiva bhūteṣu tāmasaṃ vṛttam iṣyate
english: Non-renunciation, conceit, delusion, wrath, and intolerance, and envy toward beings—such conduct is held to be of tamas.

sanskrit: vṛthārambhāś ca ye ke cid vṛthādānāni yāni ca vṛthābhakṣaṇam ity etat tāmasaṃ vṛttam iṣyate
english: Whatever undertakings are vain, and gifts that are vain, and vain eating—this conduct is held to be of tamas.

sanskrit: ativādo 'titikṣā ca mātsaryam atimānitā aśraddadhānatā caiva tāmasaṃ vṛttam iṣyate
english: Excessive speech, intolerance, jealousy, overweening pride, and faithlessness—such conduct is held to be of tamas.

sanskrit: evaṃvidhās tu ye ke cil loke 'smin pāpakarmiṇaḥ manuṣyā bhinnamaryādāḥ sarve te tāmasā janāḥ
english: Whatever men of such kind there are in this world, doers of evil who have broken the bounds of decorum—all those are people of tamas.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ yoniṃ pravakṣyāmi niyatāṃ pāpakarmaṇām avāṅnirayabhāvāya tiryaṅnirayagāminaḥ
english: I shall declare the appointed wombs of those doers of evil, who go downward into hell and to the lot of beasts and of hell:

sanskrit: sthāvarāṇi ca bhūtāni paśavo vāhanāni ca kravyādā dandaśūkāś ca kṛmikīṭavihaṃgamāḥ
english: unmoving beings, cattle, beasts of burden, flesh-eaters, biting serpents, worms, insects, and birds;

sanskrit: aṇḍajā jantavo ye ca sarve cāpi catuṣpadāḥ unmattā badhirā mūkā ye cānye pāparogiṇaḥ
english: egg-born creatures and all four-footed beings; the mad, the deaf, the dumb, and whatever others are afflicted by sinful diseases.

sanskrit: magnās tamasi durvṛttāḥ svakarmakṛtalakṣaṇāḥ avāksrotasa ity ete magnās tamasi tāmasāḥ
english: Sunk in darkness, ill-conducted, marked by what their own deeds have made them—flowing downward—these, the men of tamas, lie sunk in darkness.

sanskrit: teṣām utkarṣam udrekaṃ vakṣyāmy aham ataḥ param yathā te sukṛtāṃl lokāṃl labhante puṇyakarmiṇaḥ
english: Their rise and ascent I shall now declare hereafter—how those doers of meritorious deeds attain the worlds of the well-doing.

sanskrit: anyathā pratipannās tu vivṛddhā ye ca karmasu svakarmaniratānāṃ ca brāhmaṇānāṃ śubhaiṣiṇām
english: But those who have set out otherwise and grown great in their works—of Brāhmaṇas devoted to their own duties and seeking the good—

sanskrit: saṃskāreṇordhvam āyānti yatamānāḥ salokatām svargaṃ gacchanti devānām ity eṣā vaidikī śrutiḥ
english: by their sacraments they rise upward, striving toward fellowship of world; they go to the heaven of the gods—such is the Vedic teaching.

sanskrit: anyathā pratipannās tu vivṛddhāḥ sveṣu karmasu punarāvṛttidharmāṇas te bhavantīha mānuṣāḥ
english: But those who have set out otherwise, grown great in their own works, subject to the law of return, are born here again as men.

sanskrit: pāpayoniṃ samāpannāś caṇḍālā mūkacūcukāḥ varṇān paryāyaśaś cāpi prāpnuvanty uttarottaram
english: Having fallen into a sinful womb—as outcastes, the dumb, the deformed—they nevertheless attain the social orders in turn, each higher than the last.

sanskrit: śūdrayonim atikramya ye cānye tāmasā guṇāḥ srotomadhye samāgamya vartante tāmase guṇe
english: Passing beyond the womb of the Śūdra, those and the other qualities of tamas, gathered midway in the stream, abide within the strand of tamas.

sanskrit: abhiṣaṅgas tu kāmeṣu mahāmoha iti smṛtaḥ ṛṣayo munayo devā muhyanty atra sukhepsavaḥ
english: Attachment to objects of desire is remembered as the Great Delusion; here even seers, sages, and gods, longing for pleasure, fall into delusion.

sanskrit: tamo moho mahāmohas tāmisraḥ krodhasaṃjñitaḥ maraṇaṃ tv andhatāmisraṃ tāmisraṃ krodha ucyate
english: Tamas, delusion, the great delusion, darkness called wrath—and death is the blinding darkness; darkness is said to be wrath.

sanskrit: bhāvato guṇataś caiva yonitaś caiva tattvataḥ sarvam etat tamo viprāḥ kīrtitaṃ vo yathāvidhi
english: By its states, by its qualities, and by the wombs it leads to, in truth—all this concerning tamas, O Brāhmaṇas, has been duly proclaimed to you.

sanskrit: ko nv etad budhyate sādhu ko nv etat sādhu paśyati atattve tattvadarśī yas tamasas tattvalakṣaṇam
english: Who indeed truly understands this, who indeed truly sees it—who, perceiving the real amid the unreal, discerns the true mark of tamas?

sanskrit: tamoguṇā vo bahudhā prakīrtitā; yathāvad uktaṃ ca tamaḥ parāvaram naro hi yo veda guṇān imān sadā; sa tāmasaiḥ sarvaguṇaiḥ pramucyate
english: The qualities of tamas have been proclaimed to you in their many forms, and tamas, higher and lower, has been duly told; for the man who ever knows these qualities is released from all the qualities of tamas.
